_comment: Declarative SSOT for the internal Bugzilla (5.2) project/lifecycle configuration.
setup-projects.pl converges the installation to this state; verify-projects.py asserts it.
The IssueTypeWorkflow extension carries the same type->status/resolution/category map as
Perl constants (it must not do runtime file IO); verify-projects.py proves the two agree
behaviourally by walking both lifecycles and asserting every illegal move is rejected.
_enforcement_switch_comment: There is deliberately NO 'enforcement enabled' parameter. Any such switch would be
reachable by anyone with tweakparams, which would defeat denying administrators too.
The extension instead derives its state: cf_issue_type absent = never provisioned
(bootstrap, nothing enforced); cf_issue_type present = every ENFORCEMENT-CRITICAL part of
the model below must match, or every guarded change is refused. That means the two policy
fields' wiring, the issue types, the categories and their controllers, the resolutions,
the statuses with their is_open flags, and the whole workflow matrix. It deliberately does
NOT include cf_environment, products, components, descriptions or sort keys: those cannot
widen lifecycle policy, and the provisioner's zero-change dry run is what covers them.
Getting back to 'off' means deleting cf_issue_type, which destroys every item's type -
destructive and obvious, not a quiet toggle. From a web or API request a missing
cf_issue_type is treated as BROKEN, not as bootstrap, so deleting it is not a way out.

_comment: Bugzilla 5.2 stores ONE controller per field value (bug_status/resolution/cf_* value
tables all carry a single visibility_value_id INT2 column - see Bugzilla/DB/Schema.pm
and Bugzilla/Field/Choice.pm DB_COLUMNS). A category value therefore cannot be shared
between BUG and REQUIREMENT, which is why the vocabularies are prefixed instead.

_workflow_comment: Installation-wide matrix (bug_status + status_workflow are global in Bugzilla - there is no
per-product or per-type workflow). Both lifecycles live in this one matrix; the
IssueTypeWorkflow extension is what stops an item crossing between the two branches.
'' (empty from) is the bug-creation row (status_workflow.old_status IS NULL).
Every status must be able to reach duplicate_or_move_bug_status (RESOLVED), otherwise
Bugzilla::Status::add_missing_bug_status_transitions() re-adds the row behind our back.
_enforcement_comment: Mirrored as Perl constants in extensions/IssueTypeWorkflow/Extension.pm. Kept here so the
intended policy is reviewable in one place and so verify-projects.py can generate the
negative test cases from it rather than hard-coding them.

_allowed_categories_comment: Mirrors Extension.pm's ALLOWED_CATEGORIES. The extension compiles the vocabulary in as
well as reading each value's live controller, and requires both to agree - otherwise an
editvalues.cgi edit would silently be a policy change. setup-projects.pl asserts this
list matches the cf_category values above AND the extension's constants.
_error_codes_comment: illegal_change (115) is core Bugzilla's, raised whenever the extension denies an
UPDATE via priv_results; REST maps it to HTTP 401. The 1000xx codes are the
extension's own creation-time errors, registered through the webservice_error_codes
hook and mapped to HTTP 400. verify-projects.py asserts these exact codes so that an
auth failure, a 404 or a 500 can never be mistaken for successful enforcement.
Four of the seven are defence-in-depth rather than routinely reachable. Core's own select
validation rejects an unknown cf_issue_type before issue_type_unknown can fire (so the
verifier asserts only that creation is refused with HTTP 400 there). The two
initial_status errors are normally preempted by issue_type_workflow_misconfigured, since
a damaged workflow now trips the fail-closed state first; they remain as race defence.
verify-projects.py asserts exact codes for the reachable ones and says which it cannot
induce without deliberately damaging the installation.

decommission._comment: Opt-in only (--remove-decommissioned), and only after verification has passed. The script ABORTS if the product still holds bugs - it does not deactivate it, because a half-retired product is worse than an obvious failure. Closing bugs does not help; they must be moved to another product or deleted.
